solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get on well with upper-class sort on Polynesian island? No thanks!

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it
the exclamation tells us to refuse the 'thanks', so TA, slang for thanks, is dropped from the island

parts.note: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia
a toff is a posh, upper-class person

explanation.surface: A posh visitor to Tahiti making friends, then politely refusing something.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for 'thanks', so 'No thanks!' tells us to drop it from the island name; the toff then sits 'on' what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: two people who become friendly at once are said to have hit it off.

clue.text: Shot on target from Victor, after wicket lost

indicators.note: the wicket is lost from the word, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: a victor is the winner of a contest
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a winning shot on target after a wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery or shooting, the ring next to the bullseye is called the inner, and a shot landing there scores it.

clue.text: Free newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper given away at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: free from control, and the British daily paper of that name.

clue.text: Put past short leg by a fellow on the other side

parts.note: over can mean finished or past, as in 'the danger is over'

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: leg is taken as the word itself before cutting

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction about getting the ball past the short leg fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Short leg is a cricket fielding position near the batsman; here 'short' trims LEG to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf describes something printed on the reverse of the page you are reading.

clue.text: This clue's about gates VW's knocked over when roughly half in, half out

definitions.text: when roughly half in, half out

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five and W the cricket abbreviation for wickets, the 'gates' the clue speaks of
something knocked over has been brought down

explanation.surface: A clue about a Volkswagen crashing through gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This clue's about gates' tells us the W stands for wickets, which are small gates. A cricket team has ten wickets, so with five down the side is half batted out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, five wickets down means half of the ten possible dismissals have fallen in an innings.

clue.text: Regularly placed in drier, one dull dress or skirt

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter, starting with the first, across these words

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: putting a dull dress or skirt in the tumble drier.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirndl is a traditional Alpine full-skirted dress, or the skirt alone.

clue.text: Daughter number one beds extremely nerdish guys

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for urination, a wee

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters only of the next word

explanation.surface: A daughter who beds very nerdy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' is nursery talk for a wee, the first of the two toilet needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweebs is slang for socially awkward, boring or studious people, close to nerds.

clue.text: The Messenger runs article about …

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: about means the article is turned round

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A messenger hurrying off with an article about something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the next clue's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Messenger RNA carries genetic instructions from DNA to make proteins in a cell.

clue.text: … stupid run-out of tail-ender before end of tame draw

indicators.note: stupid suggests a muddled state, so the remaining letters are jumbled
out of says the run's letter is taken out of the tail-ender

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cricket lament: a silly run-out of the last batsman ending a tame draw.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from TAILENDER leaves TAILENDE, which 'stupid' rearranges to DELINEAT; the last letter of 'tame' completes it. 'draw' is a verb here, not a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to trace an outline, to draw or depict precisely.

clue.text: Unsettled by legside boundary

parts.note: the on side in cricket is the leg side of the field
an edge is a boundary or border

explanation.surface: A batsman nervous after a ball goes to the leg side boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervous and jittery is described with the idiom of being tense or edgy.

clue.text: Compete with second son in broadcast on TV?

parts.note: to vie is to compete

indicators.note: broadcast signals that the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve in Genesis

explanation.surface: A competition involving a second son appearing in a TV broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a programme on TV is one you can watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being shown on television is fit to be watched by viewers.

clue.text: Demolished most of prawn sandwich

indicators.note: demolished suggests something torn apart and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged
most of drops the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wolfing down most of a prawn sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of prawn' gives PRAW, which 'Demolished' rearranges; 'Demolished' looks like 'eaten' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap is a tortilla rolled around a filling, a kind of sandwich.

clue.text: Criminal, bald and in a wig? Not criminal at all

indicators.note: criminal indicates the letters are misused and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bald wearing a wig might look shady, but is entirely innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link, not fodder. 'Criminal' is the anagram signal, while the second 'criminal' sits in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Law-abiding describes someone who obeys every rule and never offends.

clue.text: Midterm Nasa outing for long- term member of CND?

indicators.note: an outing here is an excursion, sending the letters off in a new order

explanation.surface: A NASA trip during midterm for a veteran anti-nuclear campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: CND is the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, a British protest movement. The definition is playful: of its words, this is the long term.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest word in Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament is the word for giving up weapons.

clue.text: Like some poetry on iPad, rewritten in small capitals

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the printers' abbreviation for small capitals

indicators.note: rewritten means the words are written again in another order

explanation.surface: Poetry typed on an iPad and reformatted in small capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns ONIPAD into PONDAI, which goes 'in' SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondaic verse uses spondees, metrical feet of two stressed syllables.

clue.text: Spin bowler ultimately gets Pete out with one that turns

indicators.note: something that turns is moved round, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately takes the final letter of the bowler

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spin bowler finally dismisses Pete with a ball that turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin bowler' looks like one phrase, but 'Spin' alone is the definition. The R from 'bowler ultimately' is mixed with PETE, OUT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a ballet turn on one foot, a full spin of the body.

clue.text: Shot from Surrey's opener, Bill

indicators.note: opener picks the first letter, with a cricket pun on an opening batsman

parts.note: a tab is a bill or account, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A shot played by Surrey's opening batsman, named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county with a famous cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to have a stab, an attempt.

clue.text: Drew near to home

parts.note: a door pulled to is shut, so 'to' can mean shut
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: Someone getting closer to home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is no link here: a door 'pulled to' is shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To close in is an idiom for approaching or surrounding, getting steadily nearer.

clue.text: Cricketer suffering after cramp dropped willow?

indicators.note: suffering suggests something in distress, so the letters left are rearranged
dropped means the cramp's letters are removed from the cricketer

parts.note: a crick is a painful muscle cramp, as in a crick in the neck

explanation.surface: A cricketer in pain after cramp gets dropped from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing CRICK from CRICKETER leaves ETER, which 'suffering' rearranges. The question mark marks willow as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow is a kind of tree, also the wood cricket bats are made of.

clue.text: What photographers used, taking Joel Garner shot after two openers dropped

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so the remaining letters are jumbled
two openers dropped means the first two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Photographers took pictures of Joel Garner, the West Indian fast bowler, dismissing two opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping JO from JOELGARNER leaves ELGARNER for 'shot' to rearrange. Joel Garner was a West Indies fast bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlarger is a darkroom device projecting a negative to make bigger prints.

clue.text: Battle over Dunsinane hedges

indicators.note: the words hedge in, or enclose, the letters we want

explanation.surface: A battle at Dunsinane, the hill in Macbeth, fought over hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdun was a long First World War battle in 1916 between France and Germany.

clue.text: "Women like Diana avoid going topless" shock?

indicators.note: going topless removes the first letter

parts.note: to shun is to avoid
a shock is a thick mass of hair, which tresses also means

explanation.surface: Outrage at women who refuse to go topless.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting. 'shock' is hair, not surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana the goddess was a hunter, so women like her are female hunters.

clue.text: Going to the West Indies, batsman's content to be a poet

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading from right to left
content means the inside letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A batsman touring the West Indies is happy to be a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Dannie Abse was a Welsh poet. 'West Indies' looks like one place, but 'the West' signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Dannie Abse was a Welsh writer of verse and a doctor.

clue.text: In over after second over, caught an animated, prickly character

indicators.note: after places the flipped word behind the first pieces

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: over here means turned upside down, so in this down entry the word is flipped

parts.note: in taken as the word itself
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket over involving a catch, featuring a cartoon hedgehog.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'over's do different jobs: the first turns IN to NI, the second gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic the Hedgehog is a spiky blue video-game and cartoon hero.

clue.text: Deal with toad jumping around collapsing tent

indicators.note: around means the rearranged toad goes round the other letters
jumping makes the creature's letters leap into another order
collapsing shows the tent's letters fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A camping mishap: a toad hops around a tent falling down.
explanation.walkthrough: Both creatures' words are scrambled before the container step: the jumbled toad is split so that it goes 'around' the collapsed tent.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to a matter is to handle or look after it.

clue.text: What fisherman might use, taking head off fish

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: a reel holds an angler's line

explanation.surface: An angler's gear for beheading a caught fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Older woman in charge of girls playing nude against Namibia

definitions.text: Older woman in charge of girls

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the code follows
playing suggests the letters are played about with

parts.note: NA is Namibia's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A girls' team playing nude in a match against Namibia, with a chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone to young girls, originally in Spain.

clue.text: Broken left leg? That's tough, and …

indicators.note: broken means the word is shattered and its letters rearranged

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A broken leg prompts a shrug of 'tough luck', continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' is cricket's leg side, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Teflon is a hard-wearing synthetic polymer, used as a tough coating.

clue.text: … new three-quarter length sock isn't dreadfully easy to keep clean

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things badly mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
three-quarter length keeps three of the four letters, losing the first

explanation.surface: A new three-quarter-length sock that is hard to keep clean.
explanation.walkthrough: Three-quarters of SOCK is OCK; with ISNT, 'dreadfully' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface food or dirt will not cling to wipes clean with little effort.
